title: Topology: subnets and interfaces, aggregator sinkholes, ZPA App Connectors and Windows high-interaction VM credentials

prose.label: ZPA App Connectors.
prose.text: {{zpa-app-connectors}} {{zpa-app-connectors-columns}} What the Version column means for an App Connector is open {{gap:app-connector-version}}. {{zpa-app-connector-debug-logs}} {{zpa-app-connector-actions}} Whether the customer configures App Connectors is disputed {{divergence:app-connector-ownership}}.

checks.do: Whether the subnet or VLAN was passed to a decoy interface on the Decoy Connector VM before it was configured in Deception.
Which menu path an article gives for the subnet page, since Configuring a Subnet says Settings > Interfaces and Editing or Deleting a Subnet says Settings > Topology > Interfaces.
Whether a ZPA or TI subnet is being edited by the customer, since those subnets are managed by Zscaler Support.

subnet-prerequisite.statement: A subnet or VLAN must first be passed to one of the decoy interfaces on the Decoy Connector VM before it is configured in Deception.

quotes: Before you configure a subnet or VLAN, you must pass it to one of the decoy interfaces on the Decoy Connector virtual machine (VM).

subnet-vlan-id.statement: The VLAN ID field is the ID of the VLAN trunked to the selected Decoy Connector NIC and is left blank if the VLAN is untagged or no VLAN is trunked to the interface.

quotes: VLAN ID: Enter an ID for the VLAN that is trunked to the selected Decoy Connector's NIC. Keep this field blank if the VLAN is untagged or there is no VLAN trunked to the interface.

subnet-addressing.statement: Gateway/Mask takes the gateway in <Gateway-IP>/<CIDR> form (for example 192.0.2.1/24 or 192.0.2.1/255.255.255.0) and is not required when DHCP is enabled; IPv6 Gateway/Mask takes <Gateway-IPv6>/<CIDR> and is not required when IPv6 DHCP is enabled; IPv6 Enabled allows decoys in IPv6 networks, and DNS Servers is optional.

quotes: Gateway/Mask: Enter the default gateway for the VLAN or subnet with the CIDR details in the <Gateway-IP>/<CIDR> format.
These details are not required if DHCP is enabled.
IPv6 Enabled: Enable if the subnet of VLAN supports IPv6 networking. This allows you to deploy decoys in IPv6 networks.
These details are not required if IPv6 DHCP is enabled.
DNS Servers: (Optional) Enter the IP address of the DNS server that the systems in the VLAN or subnet can access.
IPv6 Gateway/Mask: Enter the default gateway for the IPv6 VLAN or subnet with the CIDR details in the <Gateway-IPv6>/<CIDR> format.

interfaces-path-short.statement: The Configuring a Subnet article gives the path as Settings > Interfaces.

quotes: Go to Settings > Interfaces.

interfaces-path-topology.statement: The edit/delete subnet article gives the path as Settings > Topology > Interfaces.

quotes: Go to Settings > Topology > Interfaces.

subnet-csv.statement: Subnet configuration can be downloaded as a CSV via Config > Download Config and re-uploaded via Config > Upload Config to add several subnets at once.

quotes: A CSV file with the subnet configuration details is downloaded.
Uploading a CSV file with subnet configuration enables you to add and configure more than one subnet at a time.
Click Config, and then select Upload Config from the drop-down menu.
Click Config, and then select Download Config from the drop-down menu.

subnet-managed-readonly.statement: Private Access (ZPA) and Threat Intelligence (TI) subnets used to deploy decoys in the Deception cloud cannot be edited or deleted by the customer; Zscaler Support manages them.

quotes: Zscaler Deception uses Private Access (ZPA) or Threat Intelligence (TI) subnets to deploy decoys in a dedicated Deception cloud. You cannot edit or delete these subnets. Contact Zscaler Support to manage them.

sinkhole-purpose.statement: When attackers connect to a decoy, they have no outbound access from it to other systems on the network or the internet; a sinkhole on an aggregator is a single point permitting outbound access from decoys to a few specified IP addresses and ports, for example for AD authentication, C2 traffic analysis or lateral movement in lab environments.

quotes: When attackers connect to a decoy, they have no outbound access from that decoy to any other systems, either from your network or the internet.
you can configure a sinkhole as a single point in your network where outbound access from the decoys to only a few specified IP addresses (systems) and services (ports) is allowed.
such as Active Directory (AD) user authentication in shared services, analysis of Command and Control (C2) traffic of malware, or permitting lateral movement in heavily controlled lab environments.

sinkhole-config.statement: A sinkhole is configured per aggregator under Settings > Topology > Aggregators with Enabled, a network, an IP within that network segment, and outbound rules of an IP address or CIDR list plus a port.

quotes: Go to Settings > Topology > Aggregators.
For IP, enter the IP address (within the network segment you have selected).
Enter an IP address or CIDR list of IP addresses.
Enter a port number.
Select Enabled.

zpa-app-connectors.statement: ZPA App Connectors are hosted by Zscaler, are configured when creating Zero Trust Network decoys, and give a secure interface between the Decoy Connector and the Zero Trust Exchange.

quotes: Private Access (ZPA) App Connectors are hosted by Zscaler and are used to connect to your Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) environment.
In the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal, App Connectors are configured when creating Zero Trust Network decoys.
Create a secure interface between the Decoy Connector and the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) via Private Access.

zpa-app-connectors-columns.statement: The ZPA App Connectors page shows ZPA Version (App Connector software), ZPA Manager Version, last connected time to the Deception Admin Portal and ZPA App Connector last connected time to the Private Access cloud.

quotes: ZPA Version: The version of the App Connector software.
ZPA Manager Version: The version of the current App Connector Manager software.
ZPA App Connector Last Connected Time: The time when the App Connector was last connected to the Private Access cloud.
Last Connected Time: The time when the Decoy Connector was last connected to the Deception Admin Portal.

zpa-app-connector-debug-logs.statement: ZPA App Connector debug logs: recent debug logs are the last 1,000 lines from each log file, all debug logs are the complete log files, the App Connector must be connected to the Admin Portal first, and the download is a .tar.xz file.

quotes: Make sure that the App Connector is connected to the Deception Admin Portal before you download the debug logs.
Request recent debug logs: Download the last 1,000 lines from each log file.
Request all debug logs: Download the complete log files.
The debug logs are downloaded and formatted in a .tar.xz file.

zpa-app-connector-actions.statement: A ZPA App Connector can be rebooted from Actions > Reboot, and its update logs are viewed by clicking Logs and selecting View update logs.

quotes: You can reboot a Private Access (ZPA) App Connector that you configured in the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.
Select the App Connector you want to reboot, and then click Actions > Reboot.
Update logs provide valuable information that you can use to troubleshoot Private Access (ZPA) App Connector update issues.
Click Logs for an App Connector to view the update logs.
Select View update logs from the drop-down menu.

windows-hi-vm-credentials.statement: Windows high-interaction VMs support Windows Server 2016, 2019 and 2022; credentials are entered as username,password with no spaces and can take up to 30 minutes to be configured by the landmine agent.

quotes: Windows Server 2016
Windows Server 2019
Windows Server 2022
Enter a username and password (separated by a comma) without any spaces.
It can take up to 30 minutes for the landmine agent to configure the credentials for Windows.

app-connector-ownership.summary: The reboot article describes an App Connector the customer configured in the Admin Portal; the connect article says the customer cannot add or connect App Connectors.

quotes: You can reboot a Private Access (ZPA) App Connector that you configured in the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.

positions.says: A Private Access App Connector is one that you configured in the Admin Portal.

quotes: You cannot add or connect the App Connectors or TI Decoy Connectors to the Deception Admin Portal yourself.

positions.says: App Connectors and TI Decoy Connectors cannot be added or connected to the Admin Portal by the customer.

app-connector-ownership.impact: An answer about whether the customer can configure, add or connect an App Connector cannot be settled from these two pages; the Admin Portal page for ZPA App Connectors says they are configured when creating Zero Trust Network decoys.

app-connector-version.title: What the Version column means for a ZPA App Connector
app-connector-version.detail: The ZPA App Connectors page describes a Version column as 'The version of the Decoy Connector' alongside ZPA Version and ZPA Manager Version. What the column means for an App Connector is not stated.
